verified_facts_vs_interpretation.verified: defender 5/6 hit@1 with a complete miss (pure noise) on the exact-identifier fixture S1, solved S3 only through 4 observed internal rewrites; challenger 5/6 hit@1 (S3 wrong-family miss), recalled the official Tavily family on S1, uniform single-call cost; no rate-limit or credential issues on the anonymous surface
verified_facts_vs_interpretation.interpretation: each provider failed a different single fixture: the native agentic path wins semantic paraphrase via hidden multi-round cost, Exa wins exact rare identifiers where the native tokenizer fails. The declared architecture (general search -> observed exact-token gap -> precision.search/Exa) is directionally supported on its declared class, but the advantage rests on ONE fixture (S1) plus a cleaner-list pattern on S0/S5 - within this benchmark's single-shot design that is not a repeated, material dominance

outcome_rationale: the benchmark supports a bounded scenario split: native search remains the default general/semantic owner (S3), while Exa demonstrates the advantage its declared role predicts on exact rare identifiers (S1) with cleaner result lists on S0/S5 and real failure-domain independence. The split is scoped: single-shot benchmark, one fixture per class, S1 page-level verification excluded by contract, and no production authority.
provisional_test_policy_implication: keep the declared architecture: general-web.search first; on an observed exact-obscure-token precision/recall gap, escalate to precision.search/Exa (anonymous hosted surface for test-stage use). Do not extend Exa's role to general semantic paraphrase search on this evidence.
